source: regional-saisonal.de, "Saisonkalender für Gemüse" and "Saisonkalender für Obst" (private German website with per-product month tables)
license: facts transcribed, page is copyright of publisher (regional-saisonal.de); no open licence stated on the pages
semantics: Three-state cells per month, taken from the img title attribute: "saisonal-regional frisch verfügbar" (fresh from domestic/regional field cultivation) -> months=true; "saisonal-regional als Lagerware verfügbar" (from domestic storage) -> stored_months=true; "nicht saisonal-regional verfügbar" -> both false. months therefore means Freiland/fresh harvest only; stored_months captures Lagerware. Greenhouse produce is not represented (e.g. tomatoes only Jul-Oct).
method: Fetched both pages with curl (plain HTML, one <table> each: 38 vegetable rows, 18 fruit rows, header + 12 month cells per row). Regex-split rows and cells, read the product name from the td.td_zutat cell (tag-stripped, HTML-unescaped) and decoded each month cell from the img title attribute. name_en assigned by hand mapping using the shared cross-region convention; compound source names such as "Bohnen, grüne" or "Blaubeeren / Heidelbeeren" mapped to a single English name.
name_en_convention: US/international names for the joinable key: eggplant, zucchini, beetroot, sweetcorn, swede, rocket, spring onion, snow pea, sweet pepper, chili pepper.
caveats: Editorial private source, not an official BLE/BZfE statistic; months reflect the site author's judgement of typical German regional availability.
Only 56 items; the vegetable table omits several common German produce (e.g. Feldsalat, Chinakohl, Knollensellerie, Rettich).
Stored months present for 13 items (root vegetables, cabbages, onions, potatoes, apples, pears, pumpkins).
